cases.exposure_context_quote: A 25-year-old previously healthy indigenous Tamang female was referred to our center following suicidal ingestion of an unknown amount of insecticide containing 30.5% imidacloprid (Nudon, India, Fig. 1)
cases.agent_quote: suicidal ingestion of an unknown amount of insecticide containing 30.5% imidacloprid (Nudon, India, Fig. 1)

symptoms.quote: On evaluation, she was disoriented [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) E4V4M4 12/15] with generalized fasciculations.
On evaluation, she was disoriented [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) E4V4M4 12/15] with generalized fasciculations.
She had a regular heart rate of 108 beats per minute, a blood pressure of 130/90 mmHg, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute
Pupils were constricted, deep tendon reflexes were normal bilaterally, and bilateral crepitations were present on auscultation.
Pupils were constricted, deep tendon reflexes were normal bilaterally, and bilateral crepitations were present on auscultation.
Unfortunately, her condition deteriorated rapidly, resulting in severe hypoxia.
4 hours later, another chest x-ray revealed bilateral infiltrates in the lower lung fields (Fig. 2). Because of aspiration pneumonitis, intravenous antibiotics
She developed hypotension on the second day of her ICU stay, which was managed with intravenous fluid boluses and vasopressors
Her ICU stay was further complicated by an episode of generalized tonic–clonic seizure on the fourth day of admission

cases.time_to_care: initial management and gastric lavage with activated charcoal elsewhere before referral; interval not stated

labs.name: arterial blood gas
labs.value: metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate levels
labs.quote: Initial arterial blood gas (ABG) showed metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate levels.

labs.name: imidacloprid concentration in body fluids
labs.quote: However, it was not feasible to detect concentrations of imidacloprid in body fluids.

treatment.name: gastric lavage with activated charcoal (before referral)
treatment.quote: referred to our center following suicidal ingestion... after appropriate initial management and gastric lavage with activated charcoal

treatment.name: atropine 0.6 mg (one cycle)
treatment.quote: She was given one cycle of 0.6 mg atropine, was intubated and shifted to the intensive care unit (ICU), where she was mechanically ventilated.

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: was intubated and shifted to the intensive care unit (ICU), where she was mechanically ventilated.

treatment.name: intravenous clindamycin 600 mg TDS and piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g TDS
treatment.quote: intravenous antibiotics (intravenous clindamycin 600 mg TDS, intravenous piperacillin tazobactam 4.5 g TDS) were started.

treatment.name: IV fluid boluses and vasopressors for hypotension
treatment.quote: She developed hypotension on the second day of her ICU stay, which was managed with intravenous fluid boluses and vasopressors

treatment.name: glycopyrrolate for copious secretions
treatment.quote: also had copious secretions, which were managed with glycopyrrolate.

treatment.name: lorazepam then intravenous levetiracetam 500 mg BD for 7 days (seizure)
treatment.quote: initially managed with injected lorazepam and then subsequently kept on intravenous levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily (BD) for 7 days.

treatment.name: haloperidol 0.25 mg (delirium)
treatment.quote: the patient was delirious and was given a low dose of haloperidol (0.25 mg).

treatment.name: oxygen supplementation after extubation for 7 days
treatment.quote: After extubation, she remained hypoxemic and required oxygen supplementation for 7 days.

cases.outcome: discharged on the tenth day of admission without residual effects
cases.outcome_quote: After a prolonged and complicated stay, she was finally discharged on the tenth day of admission without any residual effects and was well oriented.
cases.sequelae: prolonged neuropsychiatric sequela: delirium during ICU stay; later diagnosed with severe depressive episode; prescribed escitalopram 10 mg
cases.notes: Psychiatric reevaluation diagnosed severe depressive episode; patient and family counseled with psychoeducation; doing well on follow-ups.
